records.issue_text: [BUG] `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is not valid Java: `picocli` is a package name, not a class or variable, so this line does not compile. The quarkus runtime module fails to compile, breaking the entire build and every downstream artifact (CLI dist, operator image, tests). There is no static `exit(int)` on `picocli.CommandLine` either — the intended mechanism is `@Command(exitCodeOn...)` attributes or `CommandLine.execute()`'s return value, so even the intended behavior (setting a distinct process exit code) is unimplemented and `testFeatureNotEnabled` cannot assert an exit code of 4.
records.rationale: In both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, the diff adds `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);`. Here `picocli` is only referenced as a package in the import `import picocli.CommandLine;` and there is no `picocli` class/variable shown. Calling `exit` on a package name is invalid Java and would not compile, so this change introduces a build-breaking compilation error in the quarkus runtime module.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The custom image Dockerfile bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the build, but the Operator's own default deployment mechanism (the StatefulSet pods the operator creates for Keycloak CRs without a FeatureSpec) has no corresponding enablement path shown in this diff, and the docs caution says the Operator 'will fail' when the feature is off. Any operator user upgrading an existing Keycloak CR that lacks `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` hits the documented hard failure with no migration path provided in the diff (no defaulting, no CRD conversion), so existing deployments break on operator upgrade until users hand-edit their CRs.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature is enabled only in the test custom-image Dockerfile, so the flag's enablement story depends on the operator injecting --features=rolling-updates into the server build args, duplicating the feature list between the Keycloak CR FeatureSpec and the image build. The operator must now maintain the feature list in two places (FeatureSpec on the CR and whatever it bakes into kc.sh build); a user enabling rolling-updates via FeatureSpec on a prebuilt image that was built without the flag gets a server where Profile.isFeatureEnabled is false and update-compatibility exits 4, which is confusing to diagnose since the CR says the feature is on. This is the classic client+server parallel-configuration drift pattern with no single source of truth.

records.issue_text: [BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 in the same release that introduces a new exit code 4, silently redefining the wire contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` consumed by the Operator during rolling upgrades. Any operator or automation (including the operator's upgrade logic that drives UpdateStrategy and any out-of-tree scripts) written against the documented contract where exit code 4 means 'recreate upgrade required' now receives 3 — which picocli documents as an error class — so during a mixed-version rolling deploy an old operator pod evaluating a new-version server pod will misclassify 'recreate required' as a usage/software error and fail the upgrade loop instead of falling back to Recreate; nothing in this diff updates the operator's exit-code interpretation to the new values, and this cannot be disabled without a code deploy.
